ctx.x: Because there was no teacher. We only had one teacher in our whole school system for the Black kids, and we had eight schools -- one teacher. So I might see him fifteen minutes every other month in a class of sixty or better. So I was strictly on my own.

But I would listen to the guys talk about different things. And I heard them talk about a fellow who came from Milwaukee named Davani(?), a saxophone player, and they were talking about how he had, um, what in those times they called cutting everybody's head, you know, like a saxophone battle or that type of thing -- they called it a cuttin' session during those days. He had come through Jackson and cut everybody playing chord style; you know, running the chords. Most these guys might lay on a few licks, or a guy…

In the meantime, my father had left an Olerum(?) Harmony Book, which was a standard harmony book -- he left it on the piano. And I started reading this book. That's how I learned about harmony.
